answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each new identity to post a bond that existing peers co-sign, sharing liability for it. Reputation then grows like an orchard, bearing fruit only after seasons of completed, audited tasks. An attacker hoping to forge a thousand agents must lock a thousand deposits and convince honest sponsors to risk their own stake. If audits confirm what began as a whisper of coordinated fraud, every linked bond is slashed, so a cheap swarm becomes a costly loss.
